escalation_sop.docx.text:
Sales Operations — Escalation SOP (rev 3)
This standard operating procedure governs how the weekly focus review turns findings into actions.
Principles
Every recommended action must cite the playbook rule it follows. Actions that notify another team or change a commitment (supply escalations, replenishment orders, distributor calls) require a manager's approval before they are carried out; analysis and review actions do not.
When a cause is not clear
Where a brand misses target and there is no stock-out and no promotion to explain it, do not attribute a cause from the numbers alone. Commission a market check, or if nothing explains it, flag it for manual review — never invent a reason.
escalation_sop.docx.relevance_note: Relevant — defines the PENDING_APPROVAL gating rule and the 'never invent a cause' principle.

visit_note_north_feb2026.docx.text:
North Region — Market Visit Note (February 2026)
Prepared by: Regional Sales Manager, North. Circulated to sales operations.
Trade feedback
Across Jaipur and Lucknow, retailers reported that a competitor ran an unusually deep price-off campaign on mid-pack biscuits through most of February. Several stockists shifted shelf space and billing toward the competitor for the month.
Impact
Our CremeDelight range in the North lost roughly a quarter of its expected February offtake as a direct result of that competitor activity. There was no supply issue on our side and we were not running a counter-promotion, so the miss does not show up as a stock-out or a scheme in the numbers — it is entirely down to the competitor's February push.
Recommendation from the field
Consider a targeted counter-promotion or trade incentive for CremeDelight in the North next cycle.
visit_note_north_feb2026.docx.relevance_note: Relevant — documents competitor-driven CremeDelight miss in North (Feb 2026), providing context for R-03/R-06 manual-review handling.
